newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian Bourse slips slightly, turnover higher.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian Bourse slips slightly, turnover higher.

text.p: Indices on the Abidjan Stock Exchange (BVA) eased in the week to Friday, as turnover increased in the run-up to the Christmas holiday, its market report showed.

The BVA All-Share Index fell 0.06 percent to 365.80 points, pegging the 1996 rise to 31.94 percent. The 12VB 12-share index fell 1.01 percent to 249.68 points, trimming the 1996 rise to 25.30 percent.
Volume rose, with 18,061 shares traded compared with 7,084 shares the previous week. Of the shares traded, 34.61 percent were for water utility SODECI which fell 890 CFA francs to 16,960 CFA.
Other notable decliners were BLOHORN (-2,140 to 40,760 CFA) and electricity utility CIE (-950 to 13,300 CFA).
Cable maker SICABLE (+1,120 CFA to 22,620) and rubber company SOGB (+1,150 to 16,000) were the main risers.
The value of the shares traded was 314,541,400 CFA compared to 158,376,000 CFA the previous week.
The BVA index stood at 277.25 points at the end of 1995, the 12VB at 199.26 points.
The Abidjan bourse recorded a 78.57 percent rise in market capitalisation to 400 billion CFA in 1995.
